contact.lead: I'm open to full-stack, integration and automation roles, in Ireland or remote. The fastest way to reach me is email.
edu.bach.bio: I chose the technology pathway, with Physics and Technical Drawing. Philosophy, though, is what opened up my thinking: it taught me to question assumptions and look at a problem from more than one angle.
edu.bach.summary: Science track, technology pathway: the maths, physics and technical drawing that led me to engineering.
edu.daw.bio: Two years of hands-on full stack practice while finishing my degree: real work with architecture, patterns, databases, APIs, and containers. Documenting every project made me better at problem-solving.
edu.daw.p1: First year: programming (Java), databases (SQL), computer systems, markup languages and information management (HTML, XML), and development environments (IDEs, testing, refactoring and UML).
edu.daw.p2: Second year: client-side web development (JavaScript), server-side web development, deploying web applications on servers, and web interface design.
edu.daw.p3: A final web development project and on-the-job training (FCT) at Getronics, with direct contact with companies such as Deloitte, Atos, Accenture and Z1, plus career guidance and entrepreneurship.
edu.daw.summary: Advanced full-stack web development: designing, building and deploying modern applications from both the frontend and the backend.
edu.intro: Five years of engineering for the foundations, two of web development for the craft, studied at the same time as I worked.
edu.us.bio: Studying maths, electronics and programming taught me that web development was my thing: how to structure data, and how the hardware underneath fits together.
edu.us.p1: First year: programming, digital electronic circuits, physics of computing, discrete maths, calculus, linear algebra, statistics, business administration and computer structure.
edu.us.p2: Second year: design and analysis of data and algorithms, introduction to software engineering and information systems, computer logic, networks, operating systems, computer architecture and software architecture and integration.
edu.us.p3: Third year, the software engineering core: design and testing, software process and management, requirements engineering, artificial intelligence, numerical modelling, graphical modelling, multimedia signals and network services.
edu.us.p4: Fourth year: configuration management, IT project planning and management, software engineering and professional practice, and the final degree project.
edu.us.summary: Degree in Computer Engineering, Software Engineering track (240 ECTS) at the ETSII: the theory and practice of computing, from digital circuits and operating systems to requirements, design and testing.
exp.intro: I didn't take the straight road into software, and I think it shows in a good way: I've been the user, the trainer and the person on the phone with the client.

skills.title: What I work with
work.bkd: A customs platform for a private logistics client that handles GB–NI movements end to end through the API of HMRC's Trader Support Service (TSS): safety and security filings (ENS), simplified frontier and supplementary declarations, and full frontier declarations. Data comes in three ways (shipment emails read through Microsoft Graph, Excel uploads or manual entry in the portal) and is extracted, validated and pre-filled, so the team only reviews. Flask on Azure SQL, deployed with Docker.
work.butakeando: A full-stack furniture storefront for armchairs and sofas: Stripe Checkout with signed webhooks, orders that only persist once payment is confirmed, PostgreSQL and email notifications, all served as a single Docker app.
work.calendar: My own calendar, where everything else on this page meets: career milestones, certificates and birthdays, plus the tasks from Bubble, by month or by year. Swipe or scroll sideways to move through time.
work.devoo: Landing page and e-commerce frontend for DEVOO Imports, a Greek client with huge olive groves in southern Greece, introduced to me by a friend from Texas. Scroll-driven GSAP animations, with the content and catalogue loaded from JSON.
work.flow.title: Customs Operations Platform
work.gym: A monthly training plan, daily weight log and progress view. Small, fast and exactly as opinionated as I am about leg day.
work.intro: Projects for companies and individuals, and my own ones, built to learn something new or because I wanted them to exist.
work.monster: A crypto trading bot with a web3 panel: paper trading on live Binance market data, signals reviewed by Claude, on-chain balances, accounts with JWT and one-click sign-in, and a daily crypto news radar. Real trading is switched off on purpose.
work.planning: My own planner: daily focus, a weekly view, an Eisenhower matrix and a vault for decisions. Built because every to-do app I tried was either too much or too little.
work.radar: A GitHub Action wakes up every morning, reads official AI and dev-tooling feeds, and commits a JSON file. This page renders it. The bot touches data, never the layout.
work.site: React and TypeScript with SCSS, built with Vite and prerendered so it reads without JavaScript. Ten languages, light and dark themes, eight accent colours, and built automatically by GitHub Actions on every push.
work.smc: The website of Spain Motorcars, a dealer that hand-picks premium everyday cars and the odd classic: a fast single-page site with the inventory, services and buying process, in two languages and with a dark mode.
work.strattonApp: My final degree project (Web Application Development): a client-management app for an energy advisory firm, with a REST API secured with Spring Security and an Angular frontend, plus the analysis behind it: use cases, data model and prototypes.
work.sync.p1: Corporate sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID, an extra JWT layer and role-based views, with automated emails when someone is granted access to a section.
work.sync.p2: Transactions that pull tickets from an API into internal databases to monitor and analyse each person's support work, plus a built-in feedback system.
work.sync.p3: Jobs that fill missing Snowflake data straight from the SAP S/4HANA API, with report generation.
work.sync.p4: File search through SMTP logs and interface movements.
work.sync.p5: In-house AI assistant (beta): built for the company, runs without paid API tokens and resolves administrative support questions.
work.sync.summary: An internal platform for the company's support and operations teams: secure access, ticket analytics, SAP-to-Snowflake data repair and an in-house AI assistant.
work.sync.title: Support & Operations Platform
work.title: Selected work

xp.mercor.p1: Reviewed layouts, typography, spacing, slide structure and visual hierarchy so AI-generated decks were consistent and ready for professional use.
xp.mercor.p2: Spotted recurring visual issues: branding inconsistencies, chart design problems, overlapping elements and formatting defects.
xp.mercor.p3: Evaluated AI-generated writing for clarity, tone, concision and professionalism.
xp.mercor.p4: Applied structured rubrics and reference material to give evidence-based feedback, and helped calibrate AI outputs against human quality standards.
xp.mercor.summary: Improving the visual quality, consistency and professional usability of AI-generated presentations through structured evaluation and feedback.
xp.outlier.summary: As a freelancer, I created video, image, audio and text content that simulates AI-generated output, and gave human feedback used to train multimodal AI models.
xp.sap.p1: Documented the UAT and system updates for the SAP S/4HANA bonded-stock logistics system, making sure it met business needs before go-live.
xp.sap.p2: Built automated weekly Power BI dashboards that cut management’s reporting time by 30%.
xp.sap.p3: Found bottlenecks in warehouse processes and wrote clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the improved flow, which sped up new-hire training and kept the work consistent.
xp.sap.p4: Tracked risks, stock discrepancies and losses, and reported on them, contributing directly to successful internal and external audits.
xp.sap.p5: Worked with Finance to validate client billing, so order invoices were created accurately and on time in SAP S/4HANA.
xp.sap.p6: Traced the root cause of client queries about missing requirements and gave clear answers quickly, validating reports and dashboards against the source data with SQL and advanced Excel.
xp.sap.p7: Kept IT tasks on schedule by tracking dependencies, supported quarterly and annual planning, and ran Agile tracking and metrics in SharePoint and Google Sheets, coordinating the team over Microsoft Teams.
xp.sap.summary: SAP S/4HANA EWM support and warehouse process management. I optimised workflows and trained end users on the system, which helped adoption.
xp.stratton.p1: Developed advanced sales techniques and marketing strategies, helping clients achieve significant savings.
xp.stratton.p2: Mentored team members eager to learn sales methodologies.
xp.synovia.p1: Build and support full-stack integration platforms that combine frontend apps, Python/FastAPI backends, APIs, authentication, databases and cloud services.
xp.synovia.p2: Develop and maintain Azure solutions integrating Azure SQL, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Outlook and external APIs.
xp.synovia.p3: Design API-driven automation and real-time data workflows for extraction, processing, validation and database updates.
xp.synovia.p4: Contribute to logistics and customs automation with SAP EWM, TSS APIs, Snowflake, Azure Functions and Blob Storage, including automated TSS declaration workflows.
xp.synovia.p5: Build client-facing tools and operational dashboards that simplify complex workflows, give visibility over data and cut manual processing.
xp.synovia.p6: Help define architecture, repository structure, infrastructure, deployment strategy and development standards, with technical coordination and knowledge transfer across the team.
xp.synovia.summary: Working across full-stack development, integration and automation, turning operational requirements into practical software for logistics environments.
xp.sysadmin.p1: Managed order distribution in Gaina Software, system updates and shipment coordination to keep deliveries on time and on KPI.
xp.sysadmin.p2: Ran data analysis and reporting in Excel.
xp.sysadmin.p3: Improved workflows and team performance through clear communication on Microsoft Teams.
